original_question: Solved problem record: does there exist a soluble orderable group G with G/[G, G] periodic?
target_in_paper: Section 3.1 (Solved Problems), Problem 3.5: "Does there exist a soluble orderable group G with G/[G, G] periodic?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target in the paper almost verbatim: it is the existence question recorded as Problem 3.5 in Section 3.1, asking for a soluble orderable group whose quotient G/[G,G] is periodic.
missing_details: The paper places this in Section 3 on totally ordered/orderable groups; here "orderable" should be made explicit as meaning that G admits a total order invariant under both right and left multiplication.
[G,G] should be identified explicitly as the commutator subgroup of G, so that G/[G,G] is the abelianization of G.
"Periodic" should be unpacked as meaning that every element of the quotient G/[G,G] has finite order.
The problem has no extra hypotheses: there is no assumption of finite generation, countability, rank, or a specified distinguished order; it is a pure existence question over all groups.
Because the paper records this in the solved-problems section, the status note is that the answer is Yes, with reference [22]; that answer should be kept separate from the sharpened question itself.
refined_question: Does there exist a soluble group G that is orderable in the two-sided sense (that is, G admits a total order invariant under both left and right multiplication) such that its abelianization G/[G,G], where [G,G] is the commutator subgroup, is periodic, i.e. every element of G/[G,G] has finite order?
justification: This draft targets Problem 3.5 exactly, not a broader neighboring question. Section 3.1 states the problem in essentially the same words on page 18. To make it fully stand-alone, the only needed additions are the standard but implicit meanings of orderable, [G,G], and periodic. The paper's surrounding context supplies the intended notion of orderability: Section 2.1 explains that a right order is preserved by right multiplication (p. 9), and Section 3 says ordered/orderable groups are the special cases where the total order is also preserved by multiplication on the left (p. 15). I therefore kept the question narrow and did not drift to the different right-orderable finite-index problem 2.32.

citations.label: [22] V. V. Bludov, V. M. Kopytov, A. H. Rhemtulla, On normal relatively convex subgroups in soluble O-groups
